seo.title: Lacuno — Your website. Your rules.
seo.description: An open-source visual website builder in progress, designed for editable templates, static output and self-hosting.

text.value: Lacuno is an open-source website builder in progress for people who care about the craft of the page and the freedom to keep it.
A visual tool can still produce work you understand, carry and host yourself.
The planned Lacuno-operated service is intended to let people open the browser builder, start from an editable template and publish to a free subdomain with a limited page-visit allowance.
That service is future work. The durable promise is the direction: convenience should not take ownership away from the person making the site.
A simple hosted path, with self-hosting always in view.
Pages, styles, components and content stay in the Lacuno document where visual tools and agents can work with them directly.
The builder remains inspectable and self-hostable under the AGPL, so access to the work does not depend on one vendor.
Static pages keep the published result fast, comprehensible and ready for hosting in the environment you choose.
Visual building, editable source and static output belong in one clear workflow.
The web works better when your website is yours.

Lacuno is intended for designers, developers, writers and small teams who want visual composition without giving up a transparent project. The document stays structured, and the compiler produces a static website that can travel with the rest of your work.
The project is licensed under the AGPL. Users can self-host the builder and their websites, inspect how the system works and adapt it to their needs.
A browser-based builder and a Lacuno-operated hosting service are planned. They are not available capabilities today, and this template does not invent pricing, limits or a launch date.
Control is part of the design.

fields.f-title: Your website should belong to you
fields.f-summary: Why open source, portable output and the AGPL are practical choices for long-term control.

content.text: A website is more than a campaign surface. It is an archive, a storefront, a publishing system and often the first place a community meets an idea. The people who make it should be able to understand where it lives and decide what happens to it next.

Lacuno is open source under the AGPL. That commitment keeps the builder inspectable and gives teams a path to run it themselves. The same principle extends to the websites it produces: the source remains ordinary project data rather than a format held behind one service.

Ownership also changes day-to-day work. A visual editor can make composition approachable, while a static compiler can produce a site that is straightforward to serve. Designers, developers and writers can meet around one document without pretending that every discipline works in the same way.

fields.f-summary: A look at the editable document, MCP authoring and static compilation that shape Lacuno’s workflow.

content.text: Lacuno starts with a structured document. Pages, nodes, styles, components and collections stay explicit, so a visual interface and an automated collaborator can work with the same material instead of translating between private formats.

MCP exposes that document through versioned operations. A client reads the current revision, proposes or applies a defined change, and receives structured errors if the document moved or the operation is invalid. This starter site was authored through that route, which makes the workflow concrete rather than aspirational.

The compiler turns the document into static pages. Static output keeps the delivery side small and portable: the result can be served from common hosting infrastructure, inspected in a browser and moved with the rest of the project.

The browser builder is planned and is not presented here as an available service. Today, this sample article demonstrates the content model and the path from a native Lacuno document to a working website.

fields.f-title: Two ways to make it yours
fields.f-summary: How a planned hosted path and self-hosting can support different teams without changing who owns the work.

content.text: Some people want a direct path from opening a tool to publishing a site. Others need the builder and output inside infrastructure they already operate. Lacuno’s direction makes room for both without splitting the underlying document model.

A Lacuno-operated builder and hosting service are planned. The intention is to offer a convenient path to begin visually and publish to a free subdomain with a limited page-visit allowance. Exact limits, pricing and availability are not defined in this starter because the service is not implemented yet.

Self-hosting remains a first-class part of the vision. Teams should be able to run the builder and serve their websites themselves, keep their project history and choose the operational setup that fits their constraints.
Convenience and control can reinforce each other when the source stays portable. This sample article is a place to adapt that idea to your own product, community or practice.
